common.name: Name
confirm.title: Are you sure?
nav.label: Sections
login.title: Sign in
login.firstTime: Forgot your password? Ask another admin to reset it, or run “sudo -u milo milo admin-reset” on the device.
setup.title: Welcome to Milo
setup.intro: Create the owner account to finish setting up this device. You will use it to sign in from now on.
setup.usernameHint: 2-24 characters: lowercase letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter.
setup.passwordHint: At least 12 characters, known only to you. Others can be added later under Admins.
setup.mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
forced.title: Welcome, {username}
forced.intro: Choose your own password before you continue: at least 12 characters, known only to you.
buttons.intro: Each button is a physical input on a GPIO pin (BCM numbering). What it does is only this mapping - change it here, no code needed.
buttons.activeLowHint: Wired to ground with the internal pull-up (the usual way)
chats.intro: Chats are who the child can send voice messages to. The CHAT button cycles through the favorites in this order. A private chat always goes to an authorized person's own account.
people.intro: Each role has default permissions. Tick or untick a box to give one person more or less than their role; “custom” marks the differences. Deactivating someone blocks them immediately.
people.none: Nobody is authorized yet. Invite someone from the Telegram section.
telegram.turnOn: Turn Telegram on with the switch above.
telegram.tokenHelp: Every installation has its own bot. Create one with @BotFather in Telegram and paste its token here. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
telegram.pendingUrgent: {count} message(s) waiting for the child, {urgent} urgent.
telegram.inviteHelp: Create a single-use link and send it to the person. They open it in Telegram; you then approve them here. Nobody can join without an invitation and your approval.
telegram.sendNow: Send this link now - it is shown only once
telegram.noBotUsername: The bot username is not known yet (save a valid token and enable Telegram). The person can send the command above to your bot instead.
telegram.activityHelp: Only who and when. Message content is never shown here.
telegram.addAsChat: Add as a chat the child can talk to
schedules.deviceTime: Device time now: {time}. Schedules follow this timezone.
schedules.intro: Choose when each feature may be used. Messages that arrive outside the allowed hours are kept, not deleted, and announced when the hours begin. Emergency alerts always go through.
schedules.limit: Limit this feature to the hours below
schedules.blocked: No hours are set, so this feature is blocked all the time.
schedules.pickDays: Pick at least one day and both times
schedules.help: Until 00:00 means midnight. A window that ends earlier than it starts (22:00 - 06:00) continues into the next day.
assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.turnOn: Turn the assistant on with the switch above.
assistant.keysHelp: Keys are stored encrypted on the device and are never shown again. The AI service receives only what the child says as text; the speech service receives only the recording.
assistant.languageHelp: The language the assistant answers in. “Automatic” follows the language the child speaks. This is separate from the interface, notification and voice languages.
assistant.turnsLabel: Questions per hour (limits cost and free-tier use)
assistant.safetyHelp: Milo checks what the child says and what the AI answers with its own rules, on top of the AI's own safeguards. This is a safety net, not a guarantee: keep an eye on the conversations below.
assistant.checkInput: Check what the child says before the AI sees it
assistant.checkOutput: Check the AI's answers before the child hears them
assistant.alertParents: Message the parents on Telegram if the child says something worrying
assistant.followUp: Keep listening for a follow-up after each answer
assistant.providersHelp: Any OpenAI-compatible service works. Defaults: OpenRouter for the AI and Groq for speech recognition. Text-to-speech runs locally with Piper.
assistant.blockedHelp: Anything containing these is never sent to the AI or never spoken. The child hears a friendly “let's talk about something else”.
assistant.appliesBoth: What the child says and what the AI says
assistant.keptFor: Kept for {days} days, then deleted automatically.
assistant.notKept: Not kept: history is switched off.
assistant.confirmErase: Erase every stored conversation? This cannot be undone.
wakeword.title: Wake word
wakeword.turnOn: Turn the wake word on with the switch above.
wakeword.intro: Say the phrase and the assistant starts listening, without touching a button. Detection happens on the device: no audio is sent anywhere until the phrase is recognised. The buttons keep working either way.
wakeword.simulated: Development mode: use “Say the wake word” in the Simulator.
wakeword.sensitivityHelp: higher hears you more easily but may wake by mistake
wakeword.sayNow: Say “{phrase}” now, close to the device…
wakeword.samplesHelp: Record the phrase {count} times, the way it will be said in the room. More variety (near, far, quiet, loud) makes it more reliable. The built-in engine is experimental and learns the voices you record; for the best accuracy use an external neural helper.
wakeword.liveHelp: Say things near the device. Each line is how different a sound was from your samples; it wakes when the number is at or below {threshold}. Raise the sensitivity if your phrase scores above that, lower it if other words score below.
skills.timersHelp: The child (or the assistant) sets timers and reminders by voice. Turn the “timer” and “reminders” switches on above. You can add reminders here too.
skills.musicHelp: Copy .mp3 or .wav files into the music folder (for example with a USB stick or scp). The child asks “play the Frozen song”; the closest name wins. Milo keeps playing through the folder until told to stop, and a notification or spoken answer interrupts it.
skills.weatherHelp: Uses the free Open-Meteo service. Only the coordinates of your town are sent, nothing else. Turn the “weather” switch on above.
skills.calendarHelp: Read-only. Paste your calendar's secret iCalendar address (in Google Calendar: Settings → your calendar → “Secret address in iCal format”). It works like a password, so it is stored encrypted and never shown again. Repeating events are supported; unusual repeat rules may be missed. Event titles are read aloud and, when the assistant reads them, sent to the AI service.
sound.help: Speaker volume is changed with the volume buttons (set_volume action) or by voice. Test the hardware on the device with: milo test-audio
sound.notificationsHelp: Sounds never reveal who wrote or what. A short “piii” means a message is waiting; three long tones mean an emergency.
sound.newMessage: Play a sound for new messages
sound.afterHours: Announce messages that arrived outside usage hours when hours begin
wifi.title: Wi-Fi
wifi.help: The device joins the highest-priority network it can see. Add your home, your grandparents' and a phone hotspot. Passwords are stored encrypted. You need Internet access on the Pi for the first setup.
wifi.name: Network name
system.languagesHelp: The interface language is used by this admin page. The notification language is the default for messages Milo sends people (people can have their own in the People section). The assistant and voice languages are set in the Assistant section.
system.announceSender: Say who a message is from before playing it
system.audioHelp: The defaults suit the Waveshare WM8960 HAT. List sound cards on the device with: aplay -l
system.speaker: Speaker
system.saved: Saved. Restart Milo to apply the button and audio settings.
system.restartHelp: Restarts the Milo program (not the whole Raspberry Pi). It is back within a few seconds.
system.restarting: Restarting… reload this page in a few seconds.
system.logHelp: The latest events since Milo started. Secrets and message contents never appear here.
backup.downloadHelp: One encrypted file with everything: settings, family, messages, conversations and the encrypted secrets. Keep it on a USB stick or in your cloud storage - without the passphrase nobody can read it. A memory card can fail without warning, so make a copy now and after big changes.
backup.passphraseLabel: Passphrase (at least {min} characters - write it down!)
backup.includeKey: Include the master key (needed to rebuild the device on a new card)
backup.downloaded: Backup downloaded. Keep the file and the passphrase somewhere safe.
backup.restoreHelp: Choose a backup file and enter its passphrase. Milo checks it first and changes nothing until you restart. This works for backups made by this device. To move a backup to a new device or a new memory card, use the command line: sudo systemctl stop milo; sudo milo restore FILE --replace-key
backup.readyHelp: “{name}”, made {when}. It replaces everything on this device (settings, family, messages and administrator accounts) when Milo restarts. The current data is kept aside on the device.
backup.restarting: Restarting… sign in again in a few seconds.
backup.automaticHelp: Milo keeps a few recent copies of its database so a damaged file can be recovered. They live on the same memory card, so they do not replace a downloaded backup. They are not encrypted (they contain what the database contains) and never contain the master key.
admins.passwordHelp: Choose a long password only you know (at least 12 characters). Changing it signs you out of other browsers.
admins.revealHelp: Give this to them now. It is shown only once, and they must choose their own when they first sign in.
admins.title: Administrators
admins.help: Everyone listed here can manage the device from this page. Only the owner can add, reset or remove them.
admins.addHelp: For example mom, dad or grandma. A password is generated and shown once; they choose their own at first sign-in.
simulator.title: Virtual device
simulator.help: Development mode: no real hardware is used. Press the buttons like a child would.
simulator.wakeHelp: Pretend someone said the wake phrase (needs the “wakeword” feature on).
simulator.sayHint: What the child says next, e.g. Set a timer for one minute
simulator.armed: Ready: press the talk / GPT button now
simulator.micHelp: The next recording will contain this sentence.
simulator.speaker: Speaker
home.title: What would you like to do?
home.subtitle: Pick a tile to see it and change it.
home.setup.title: Finish setting up
home.step.telegram.hint: Create a bot with @BotFather and paste its token.
home.step.people.hint: Send them an invitation link from the Telegram section.
home.step.assistant.hint: Add an AI key so Milo can answer questions.
home.step.wifi.hint: So Milo stays online when you move it.
needs.telegramToken: Add your bot token to start Telegram.
needs.assistantKey: Add the AI key to start the assistant.
needs.wakeSamples: Record a few samples of the wake phrase to start.
prompt.telegram.title: Connect Telegram
prompt.telegram.intro: Every installation has its own bot. Create one with @BotFather in Telegram and paste its token here. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
prompt.assistant.title: Add the assistant's keys
prompt.assistant.intro: Keys are stored encrypted on the device and are never shown again. You can change the rest later in the Assistant section.
setup.doneBody: Your username is shown below. You will need it, with your password, every time you sign in.
login.hint: Your username is the name you chose during setup, for example “mom” or “dad”.
people.remoteHint: To let someone manage Milo from Telegram while away, give them the permissions below: manage configuration (status and volume), manage users (access requests), manage features and manage schedules. They will then see an Administration button in the bot.
people.forward: Send me a copy of messages left for the device
people.forwardHint: Only for people who can manage users. Off by default. The copy arrives in this person's Telegram with who sent it and when; the sender is not told each time.
skills.placeSearchPrivacy: While you type, the text is sent to Open-Meteo's place search, and your internet address is checked once every few hours to show places in your country first. Places elsewhere appear too, so a VPN does not get in the way.
skills.detectPrivacy: Uses your internet address once to find your area; nothing is stored except the place. It is approximate: type your town to correct it.
needs.weatherPlace: Choose your town to start the weather.
prompt.weather.title: Where do you live?
prompt.weather.intro: The weather needs to know your area. Milo can find it for you, or you can type your town.
prompt.weather.needTown: Type your town, or use “Detect my location”.
spotify.title: Spotify
spotify.about: Milo shows up as a speaker in the Spotify app. Open Spotify on a phone, tap the devices button and pick Milo: the music plays on this device. Spotify Premium is required.
spotify.unofficial: This uses go-librespot, an unofficial Spotify client that Spotify does not endorse and could break at any time. Milo does not include it: you install it yourself.
spotify.installSteps: Download the linux_arm64 release from github.com/devgianlu/go-librespot/releases, copy the go-librespot file to that path, make it executable and turn Spotify off and on again. The full steps are in docs/spotify.md.
spotify.pairIntro: Link the Spotify account that has Premium. Milo never sees the password.
spotify.pairStep2: 2. Sign in and type this code:
spotify.useIt: In the Spotify app, tap the devices button and pick “{name}”.
spotify.signOutConfirm: Milo will forget this Spotify account. You can pair it again later.
spotify.voiceControl: Let the assistant control Spotify by voice (pause, next, previous, play a playlist)
spotify.voiceWarning: Spotify’s developer policy restricts voice control of Spotify, and this uses go-librespot’s unofficial local interface. It is off by default and is at your own risk. Asking Milo to stop or pause always works, and the assistant can only play your own playlists, not search Spotify.
